source_text: κύριος». 27.66 τοῦ οὖν ἢ πῶς ἢ πότε τοσαύταις ἐναργέσι τε καὶ ἰσοτρόποις καὶ ἀπαραλλάκτοις τοῦ πατρὸς τετιμημένος χρῃσμωδίαις ἀνόμοιος εἰσκομισθείη; 28.ν Περὶ τοῦ τὸν υἱὸν πᾶν ἀγαθὸν ἀνατέλλειν καὶ εἶναι «ἥλιον δικαιοσύνης καί ἴασιν» καί «θησαυρὸν σοφίας καὶ γνώσεως» καί «φῶς», καὶ τοὺς πιστεύ οντας καί «μὴ σκανδαλιζομένους εἰς αὐτόν» «υἱοὺς φωτὸς γίνεσθαι». 28.1 Οἱ γοῦν περὶ αὐτοῦ ὑμνηκότες διαφόρως ἡμῖν τὴν θεότητα αὐτοῦ καὶ τὸ τελέως αὐτὸν προεστάναι τῶν οἰκείων ἔργων ἐπιδεικνύντες διδάσκουσιν, ὅτι αὐτός ἐστι παντὸς ἀγαθοῦ παρεκτικὸς καὶ φῶς ἀγαθοειδὲς καὶ ἀγαθοποιὸν καὶ ἥλιος νοητός, τῷ ἀφ' ἑαυτοῦ ἀλήκτῳ φωτὶ ἀπολαμπρύνων τὰ ὄμματα τῶν ἀπλανῶν καὶ δεκτικῶν ψυχῶν καὶ εἴσω τῆς νοητῆς ἄγων περιωπῆς καὶ ποιῶν ὁρᾶν, ἃ μὴ πρότερον δι' ἁμαρτίας ὁρᾶν καθ' αὑτὰ ἐπεφύκει, ἢ καὶ ὅλον τὸν ἄρτιον ἄνθρωπον φωτοειδῆ ποιῶν, ὡς ὁ ἥλιος ἡλιοειδῆ τὰ σώματα τὰ ἐν οἷς παραγίνεται· ἔτι δὲ ὅτι καὶ ἴασις καί «θησαυρὸς σοφίας καὶ γνώσεως» ἀδαπάνητος καὶ πανταρκὴς τυγχάνει. 28.2 Καὶ οἱ περὶ αὐτὸν εἰλικρινῶς διακείμενοι ὡς καὶ περὶ τὸν πατέρα αὐτοῦ υἱοὶ φωτὸς γίνονται καθὰ υἱοὶ τοῦ θεοῦ πατρός, ὡς ἡνίκα διακηρύττουσιν Μαλαχίας μέν· «ἀνατελεῖ ὑμῖν τοῖς φοβουμένοις τὸ ὄνομά μου ἥλιος δικαιοσύνης, καὶ ἴασις ἐν ταῖς πτέρυξιν αὐτοῦ»· 28.3 Πέτρος δὲ ἐν τῇ δευτέρᾳ ἐπιστολῇ· «ἕως οὗ ἡμέρα διαυγάσῃ καὶ φωσφόρος ἀνατείλῃ ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις ὑμῶν»· 28.4 ἔλεγεν δέ, οἶμαι, τὸν ἀπὸ τῆς δευτέρας αὐτοῦ ἐπιφανείας ἀνίσχειν μέλλοντα ταῖς ψυχαῖς φωτισμὸν καὶ πάντα καταφαιδρύνοντα τὰ σκότῳ κεκρατημένα· 28.5 καὶ ἑτέρωθι· «καὶ ἡ δόξα κυρίου ἐπὶ σὲ ἀνατέταλκεν»· 28.6 33 Ζαχαρίας δὲ προεφήτευσεν· «εἴ τι ἀγαθόν, αὐτοῦ, καὶ εἴ τι καλόν, παρ' αὐτοῦ ἔσται». 28.7 καὶ Παῦλος πρὸς μὲν Κολοσσαεῖς περὶ αὐτοῦ ἔφη· «ἐν ᾧ εἰσιν πάντες οἱ θησαυροὶ τῆς σοφίας καὶ γνώσεως ἀπόκρυφοι», πρὸς δὲ Ῥωμαίους· «λέγει γάρ», φησίν, «ἡ γραφή· πᾶς ὁ πιστεύων ἐπ' αὐτῷ οὐ καταισχυνθή σεται. οὐ γάρ ἐστι διαστολὴ Ἰουδαίου καὶ Ἕλληνος· ὁ γὰρ αὐτὸς κύριος πάντων πλουτῶν εἰς πάντας τοὺς ἐπικαλουμένους αὐτόν. πᾶς γάρ, ὃς ἂν ἐπικαλέσηται τὸ ὄνομα κυρίου, σωθήσεται». 28.8 ποῖον δὲ ὄνομα ἐπικαλοῦνται τοῦ υἱοῦ, οἱ μηδὲ θεὸν ἄκτιστον μηδὲ υἱὸν ὁμοούσιον τῷ πατρὶ λέγοντες αὐτὸν τὸν καλλίνικον, τὸν σωτῆρα οὐρανοῦ καὶ γῆς καὶ θαλάσσης; 28.9 Καὶ Ἰωάννης ὁμοίως περὶ αὐτοῦ· «ὡς τὸ φῶς ἔχετε, πιστεύετε εἰς τὸ φῶς, ἵνα υἱοὶ φωτὸς γένησθε». 28.10 μετὰ γὰρ θάνατον, φησίν, μετάνοια οὐκ ἔστιν, ὡς καὶ ∆αυῒδ ψάλλει· «ἐν δὲ τῷ ᾅδῃ τίς ἐξομολογήσεταί σοι;» καὶ πάλιν ἀπὸ τοῦ σωτῆρος· «πορευθέντες ἀπαγγείλατε Ἰωάννῃ, ἃ βλέπετε καὶ ἀκούετε· τυφλοὶ ἀνα βλέπουσιν, χωλοὶ περιπατοῦσιν καὶ νεκροὶ ἐγείρονται καὶ πτωχοὶ εὐαγγελί ζονται· καὶ μακάριός ἐστιν ὃς ἐὰν μὴ σκανδαλισθῇ ἐν ἐμοί». 28.11 Τί γὰρ λέξει περὶ τῶν πλανωμένων καὶ τῶν πλανώντων; 28.12 Ἠσαΐας προεῖπεν· «λαός μου, οἱ μακαρίζοντες ὑμᾶς πλανῶσιν ὑμᾶς καὶ τὴν τρίβον τῶν ποδῶν ὑμῶν ταράσσουσιν. ἀλλὰ νῦν καταστήσεται εἰς κρίσιν κύριος καὶ στήσει τὸν λαὸν εἰς κρίσιν. αὐτὸς κύριος εἰς κρίσιν ἥξει μετὰ τῶν πρεσβυτέρων τοῦ λαοῦ καὶ μετὰ τῶν ἀρχόντων αὐτοῦ. ὑμεῖς δὲ τί ἐνεπυρίσατε τὸν ἀμπελῶνά μου;». 28.13 ἥξει δὲ αὐτὸς κύριος εἰς κρίσιν μετὰ τῶν διδασκάλων καὶ ἀρχόντων, οὐχ ὡς αὐτὸς ὑπ' ἄλλου κριθησόμενος, ἀλλ' ὡς ἐλέγξων αὐτούς, καθάπερ διαλαλεῖ ἐν ἄλλῳ μέρει· «δεῦτε καὶ διακριθῶμεν, λέγει κύριος, οἷα», φησίν, «τὰ ἀπ' ἐμοῦ ὑπῆρξεν ὑμῖν καὶ οἷα τὰ ἀφ' ὑμῶν γέγονεν εἰς ἐμὲ καὶ τοὺς δούλους μου». 28.14 λέγει γάρ «ἀμπελῶνα» τὸν κόσμον ἢ τὸν λαόν, ὅντινα οἱ μὲν αἱρετικῶν καὶ Ἰουδαίων ἐξηγηταὶ διὰ τῆς βλασφήμου διδασκαλίας ἔνοχον ἐποίησαν τῷ τῆς γεέννης πυρί, οἱ δ' ἄρχοντες, οὐκ οἰκειωσάμενοι τὰ κατ' αὐτόν, ἀποχρησάμενοι δὲ τῇ ἐξουσίᾳ, ποικίλως καὶ διαφόρως ἠδίκησαν. 28.15
pass_a_gloss: [... is of all] Lord'. 27.66 On what ground then, or how, or when, could he who has been honoured with so many clear and like-mannered oracles, not differing from those of the Father, be brought in as unlike? 28.ν [Chapter title:] About the Son making every good rise, and being 'sun of righteousness and healing' and 'treasure of wisdom and knowledge' and 'light', and about those who believe and 'are not made to stumble into him' 'becoming sons of light'. 28.1 Those at any rate who have sung hymns about him, showing us in various ways his Godhead and his presiding perfectly over his own works, teach that he himself is the provider of every good, and a light good in form and good-doing, and a sun perceived by the mind, making bright with the unceasing light from himself the eyes of souls that do not wander and are receptive, and leading them within the intelligible lookout, and making them see the things which before, through sin, they were not by nature able to see by themselves; or even making the whole complete man light-formed, as the sun makes sun-formed the bodies in which it comes to be present; and further that he also happens to be healing and an inexhaustible and all-sufficient 'treasure of wisdom and knowledge'. 28.2 And those sincerely disposed toward him, as also toward his Father, become sons of light, as being sons of God the Father, as when Malachi proclaims: 'for you who fear my name a sun of righteousness will rise, and healing in his wings'; 28.3 and Peter in the second letter: 'until day dawns through and a light-bearer rises in your hearts'; 28.4 and he was speaking, I think, of the illumination that is going to rise on souls from his second appearing and to make bright all the things held fast by darkness; 28.5 and elsewhere: 'and the glory of the Lord has risen upon you'. 28.6 [page number 33] And Zechariah prophesied: 'if anything is good, it is his, and if anything is beautiful, it will be from him'. 28.7 And Paul said about him to the Colossians: 'in whom are all the treasures of the wisdom and knowledge hidden', and to the Romans: 'for the Scripture says', he says, 'everyone who believes on him will not be put to shame. For there is no distinction of Jew and Greek; for the same Lord of all is rich toward all who call on him. For everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved'. 28.8 But what name of the Son do they call on, those calling him, the glorious victor, the Saviour of heaven and earth and sea, neither uncreated God nor Son of the same substance as the Father? 28.9 And John likewise about him: 'as you have the light, believe into the light, so that you may become sons of light'. 28.10 For after death, he says, there is no repentance, as also David sings: 'but in Hades who will confess to you?'; and again from the Saviour: 'having gone, report to John the things you see and hear: blind people see again, lame people walk, and dead people are raised, and poor people have good news preached to them; and blessed is whoever is not made to stumble in me'. 28.11 For what will he say about those being led astray and those leading astray? 28.12 Isaiah foretold: 'my people, those who call you blessed lead you astray and throw the path of your feet into confusion. But now the Lord will take his stand for judgment and will set the people for judgment. The Lord himself will come to judgment with the elders of the people and with its rulers. But you, why did you set fire to my vineyard?' 28.13 And the Lord himself will come to judgment with the teachers and rulers, not as being himself about to be judged by another, but as about to convict them, just as he speaks out in another part: 'come and let us be judged against each other, says the Lord; what sort of things', he says, 'came to you from me and what sort have been done by you toward me and my servants'. 28.14 For he calls 'vineyard' the world or the people, which the interpreters of heretics and Jews made liable to the fire of Gehenna through blasphemous teaching, while the rulers, not making its affairs their own but misusing their authority, wronged in many and various ways. 28.15 [the paragraph number ends the section; its text begins in the next section]
pass_b_english: … Lord” (Acts 10:36). On what ground, then, or how, or when could he be brought in as unlike the Father, when he has been honoured with so many oracles, so clear, so alike in manner, and in no way different from those spoken of the Father?

That the Son makes every good thing dawn, and is “the sun of righteousness and healing,” “the treasure of wisdom and knowledge,” and “light”; and that those who believe and “are not made to stumble in him” “become sons of light.”

Those, at any rate, who have sung his praises show us his Godhead in various ways, and that he presides in full over his own works. They teach that he is the giver of every good: a light good in form and doing good, a sun seen by the mind. With the unceasing light that comes from himself he makes bright the eyes of souls that do not wander and are ready to receive him. He leads them within the vantage point of contemplation and makes them see what, because of sin, they could not see before by their own nature; or he even makes the whole perfected man full of light, as the sun makes sunlike the bodies it comes upon. They teach, further, that he is also healing, and an inexhaustible and all-sufficient “treasure of wisdom and knowledge.”

And those who are sincerely disposed toward him, as toward his Father, become sons of light, since they are sons of God the Father. So Malachi proclaims: “For you who fear my name the sun of righteousness will rise, and healing in his wings” (Malachi 4:2). And Peter in his second letter: “Until the day dawns and the morning star rises in your hearts” (2 Peter 1:19). He meant, I think, the illumination that is to rise on souls at his second appearing and to make bright all that darkness holds fast. And elsewhere: “And the glory of the Lord has risen upon you” (Isaiah 60:1).

Zechariah prophesied: “If anything is good, it is his; and if anything is beautiful, it will come from him” (Zechariah 9:17). And Paul said of him to the Colossians: “In whom all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge are hidden” (Colossians 2:3); and to the Romans: “For the Scripture says,” he writes, “‘Everyone who believes in him will not be put to shame.’ For there is no distinction between Jew and Greek; for the same Lord of all is rich toward all who call on him. For everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved” (Romans 10:11-13).
But what name of the Son do they call on, who call him, the glorious victor, the Saviour of heaven and earth and sea, neither uncreated God nor Son of one substance with the Father?

John likewise says of him: “While you have the light, believe in the light, so that you may become sons of light” (John 12:36). For after death, he says, there is no repentance, as David too sings: “But in Hades who will confess to you?” (Psalm 6:5). And again, from the Saviour: “Go and tell John what you see and hear: the blind receive their sight, the lame walk, the dead are raised, and the poor have the good news preached to them; and blessed is whoever is not made to stumble in me” (Matthew 11:4-6).

For what will he say about those who are led astray and those who lead them astray? Isaiah foretold it: “My people, those who call you blessed lead you astray and confuse the path of your feet. But now the Lord will take his stand for judgment and will set his people for judgment. The Lord himself will come to judgment with the elders of the people and with their rulers. But you, why did you set my vineyard on fire?” (Isaiah 3:12-14).

The Lord himself will come to judgment with the teachers and rulers, not as one who is himself to be judged by another, but to convict them, as he declares in another place: “Come, and let us go to judgment, says the Lord” (Isaiah 1:18): “what things,” he says, “came to you from me, and what things have been done by you to me and to my servants.”

For he calls the world, or the people, a “vineyard.” The interpreters of the heretics and of the Jews made it liable to the fire of Gehenna by their blasphemous teaching; and the rulers, who did not make its welfare their own concern but abused their authority, wronged it in many and various ways.

lemmas.gloss: interrogative genitive (Attic τοῦ = τίνος): on what ground, why

choices.issue: Old draft garbled and printed edition numbers
choices.choice: Retranslated the whole section from the Greek. The old English printed '28.n', '28.1'-'28.7' and the page number '33' (as '28.6 33') inside the sentences, ran the chapter title into the first paragraph, turned 27.66 into 'how could you be inserted into ... oracles', garbled 28.4 ('the one from his second appearance is about to rise to the souls as a light'), doubled 'for he says, he says' and gave 'believing upon it' in 28.7, read καλλίνικον as 'the fine net' and reversed the sense of the question in 28.8, and made the vineyard 'guilty ... regarding the fire' in 28.14. References: abbreviations (Mal, Col, 2 Pet, Rom, Matt, Isa) written in full; Romans 10:11 and 10:12-13 joined as Romans 10:11-13; Isaiah 43:26 corrected to Isaiah 1:18 (Didymus quotes the 'Come ... says the Lord' of 1:18); Acts 10:36 added for the closing word of the previous quotation.

choices.why: The section opens with the last word of Acts 10:36 (“he is Lord of all”), begun in the previous section. Only the word this section holds is translated, with a leading ellipsis.

choices.term: τοῦ οὖν ἢ πῶς ἢ πότε
choices.english: On what ground, then, or how, or when
choices.why: τοῦ is read as the Attic interrogative genitive (= τίνος, 'why, on what ground'), which fits the run of three questions.

choices.english: be brought in as unlike the Father
choices.why: ἀνόμοιος is the Anomoean slogan ('unlike'); 'the Father' is supplied from the genitive τοῦ πατρός just before, which English needs to make 'unlike' complete. Not bracketed: the comparison is in the Greek.
περιωπή is a lookout or height from which one sees around; νοητή makes it a height of the mind. 'Inward contemplation' in the old draft lost the image.

choices.english: a sun seen by the mind
choices.why: νοητός in its Platonic sense, the sun of the intelligible world, as against the bodily sun of the next clause.
καλλίνικος, 'gloriously victorious', a title of Christ; the old 'fine net' misread the word.
The Nicene term; kept as the house rendering used elsewhere in this work.
Used in both the chapter title and Matthew 11:6 so the reader sees the title points to that verse.
LXX ἐξομολογέομαι means both praise and confess; Didymus draws the verse in to show there is no repentance after death, so 'confess' keeps his point.

choices.term: οὐκ οἰκειωσάμενοι τὰ κατ' αὐτόν, ἀποχρησάμενοι δὲ τῇ ἐξουσίᾳ
choices.english: who did not make its welfare their own concern but abused their authority
choices.why: αὐτόν refers back to the vineyard (the people); ἀποχράομαι with ἐξουσία means misuse, not merely 'make use of'.

Words split by line breaks in the copy-text (πιστεύ οντας, καταισχυνθή σεται, ἀνα βλέπουσιν, εὐαγγελί ζονται) read as single words; the printed page number '33' after 28.6 and the bare paragraph number '28.15' at the end of the section are skipped.
